title: A 24 point icon shows at 32 and 48 beside the artboard too
goal: The preview strip beside an icon frame only shows sizes at or below the frame's own, so a 24 point icon shows at 16 and 24 and never at 48, which the icon success list and the drawing walkthrough both promise. Designers check a 24 icon at 32 and 48 as well, on a dark chip for one of them, as the mock draws.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-draw-wt.html #igSizes step 11 (16, 24, 32, 48 with 32 on a dark chip). Answered card see-an-icon-at-the-size-it-will-really-be-used ('strip') promised 16 to 64. Code: Sources/PhotonzCore/IconPreviews.swift sides(forFrameSide:) ~51-56 deliberately keeps only sizes at or below the frame ('Nothing bigger'), test pins it at Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/IconPreviewTests.swift:44 (expects [16, 24]). Chips all use .fill(.quaternary) in Sources/Photonz/IconPreviewsStrip.swift chip(). The mock is the floor: change the rule, update the test first.
acceptance: A new 24 point icon frame at Next defaults shows previews at 16, 24, 32 and 48, updating as you draw
One chip is dark as in icon-draw-wt.html step 11, so a light glyph can be checked
16 and 32 point frames show the sizes the mock implies for them, and the rule is written in the audit
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the strip beside the mock; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Adversarial pass before building: icon frames get a white surface by default, so a dark chip drawn as Export draws it would be a white square with a dark rim; and a black glyph on near black reads as nothing. Mock draws the glyph light on the dark chip (currentColor template). So the dark chip drops the frame surface and turns a one colour dark grey glyph light; coloured icons are shown as drawn.

Rule (in IconPreviews.sides): every interface size up to twice the frame's own, plus its own when 64 or under. 16 -> 16,24,32; 24 -> 16,24,32,48; 32 and up -> 16..64. Dark chip is the one before the biggest (IconPreviews.darkSide): 32 under a 24, 24 under a 16, 48 under 32+. Light chips are painted the frame's own flat surface (iconPreviewGroundHex) while the picture stays byte-exact export: dropping the white from light pictures was tried and measured up to 50/255 darker AA edges on screen (CI blends linear, SwiftUI in sRGB), which would flatter hairlines.

Tests: full Scripts/test.sh hung twice at 0% CPU (HEIF writer + AVAssetReader, logged on find-out-why-the-whole-test-run-hangs-in-the-mac). Ran split instead: --skip Render|Media 11009 pass; Render minus PackageIO|ImageCodec|Sound|Peaks|Read|HEIF 999 pass. Media and those render suites untouched by this change. Walks: icon-previews-dark-chip-walk (new, Next defaults, no flags), icon-previews-stay-with-nothing-picked-walk (24 and 48 expectations updated), icon-preview-walk, motion-loop-preview-walk all ok.

left rough: the dark chip's soft edges blend in sRGB on screen, so a hairline there reads slightly heavier than the same line would composited by the renderer; there is no exported equivalent of the dark chip to be true to, so not filed. Also a walk cannot set a shape's colour, so the light-on-dark glyph is proved by unit tests only; not filed (no one using the app notices).

A 24 point icon frame now previews at 16, 24, 32, 48 with the 32 on the mock's near black chip (glyph turned light there when drawn in one dark grey); a 16 shows 16, 24, 32; 32 and up show 16 to 64. Light chips are painted the frame's surface so the glyph sits on the chip, picture byte-exact export. Commit 335d0d38. Verified: new walk icon-previews-dark-chip-walk at Next defaults plus 3 updated/neighbour walks ok; tests split (full run hangs, see hang task): 11009 + 999 pass. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-10-icon-previews-sizes.json.
